Evaluate the safety of eliglustat (by serious adverse event continuous monitoring), the quality of life (Short Form-36 Health Survey \[SF-36\]) and biomarkers of Gaucher disease type 1 (GD1) (chitotriosidase, plasma glucosylceramide \[GL-1\] and lyso glucosylceramide \[lyso-GL-1\]) in adult participants who successfully completed one of the Phase 2 or Phase 3 studies.

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for Gaucher disease
Open Targets drugs acting on GBA1
Discovery of Brain-Penetrant Glucosylceramide Synthase Inhibitors with a Novel Pharmacophore.
papers.summary: The paper reports the discovery of brain-penetrant inhibitors of glucosylceramide synthase (GCS), identifying T-036 as a potent inhibitor in vivo and T-690 as a lower-toxicological-risk inhibitor that reduced glucosylceramide dose-dependently in mouse plasma and cortex. The study positions GCS inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for Gaucher disease and as a potential strategy for Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Adverse Event Profile Differences Between Eliglustat and Miglustat: A Pharmacovigilance Study using the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System.
papers.summary: The paper identifies eliglustat and miglustat as substrate reduction therapies that target glucosylceramide synthase, establishing this biosynthetic mechanism as a clinically actionable target. The study also reports drug-specific and sex-associated adverse-event signals, but the abstract does not explicitly name Gaucher disease or provide mechanistic outcomes beyond target engagement.

papers.title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of Oral Venglustat in Patients with Parkinson's Disease and a GBA Mutation: Results from Part 1 of the Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled MOVES-PD Trial.
papers.summary: In a small phase 2 trial of 29 patients with Parkinson’s disease and heterozygous GBA mutations, oral venglustat was brain-penetrant and dose-dependently reduced plasma and cerebrospinal-fluid glucosylceramide, demonstrating central inhibition of glucosylceramide synthase and target engagement. The study found generally acceptable short-term tolerability but no short-term symptomatic benefit, and it was not designed to establish disease modification or efficacy.
papers.why: A phase II trial provides human safety, pharmacokinetic, and target-engagement data for brain-penetrant substrate reduction in GBA1-mutant disease.

papers.title: Preclinical pharmacology of glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat in a GBA-related synucleinopathy model.
papers.summary: The brain-penetrant glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat engaged its target in GBA-mutant mouse models and reduced glucosylceramide, glucosylsphingosine, and hippocampal protein aggregates. In the homozygous GbaD409V/D409V Gaucher-related synucleinopathy model, long-term treatment also ameliorated a novel-object-recognition memory deficit, although clinical GCS inhibition did not alter disease progression in early GBA-associated Parkinson’s disease.

papers.title: Glucosylceramide synthase inhibition alleviates aberrations in synucleinopathy models.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: The paper shows that the brain-penetrant glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor GZ667161 reduces CNS glucosylceramide and glucosylsphingosine and improves α-synuclein-related pathology and behavioral outcomes in two murine synucleinopathy models. These findings support glucosylceramide synthase inhibition as a disease-modifying strategy for GBA-related synucleinopathies, although efficacy in patients or sporadic disease was not established.

papers.title: Safety and efficacy of venglustat in GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease: an international, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
papers.summary: In a 52-week phase 2 trial, venglustat, an inhibitor of glucosylceramide synthase, produced no beneficial effect on MDS-UPDRS parts II and III scores in people with early-stage GBA1-associated Parkinson's disease. The findings suggest that inhibiting glucosylceramide synthase may not be a viable therapeutic approach for this population.

papers.title: Miglustat: substrate reduction therapy for glycosphingolipid lysosomal storage disorders.
papers.summary: This review describes miglustat as a substrate-reduction treatment for glycosphingolipid lysosomal storage disorders, including type 1 Gaucher disease. It states that miglustat inhibits processing enzymes including ceramide-specific glucosyltransferase, thereby targeting the initial committed step of glycosphingolipid synthesis, but the abstract provides no new intervention results.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Tolerability of Single-Dose Orally Administered Venglustat in Healthy Chinese Volunteers.
papers.summary: A phase I study showed that a single 15 mg oral dose of the brain-penetrant glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat had a favorable pharmacokinetic, safety, and tolerability profile in 14 healthy Chinese volunteers. The trial did not measure pharmacodynamic effects such as plasma glucosylceramide, so direct suppression of glucosylceramide synthesis was not demonstrated in the studied population.

papers.title: Pyrazole Ureas as Low Dose, CNS Penetrant Glucosylceramide Synthase Inhibitors for the Treatment of Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: The paper reports optimization of bicyclic pyrazole urea inhibitors of glucosylceramide synthase (GCS) into low-dose, oral, CNS-penetrant compounds with in vivo activity in mouse models and ex vivo activity in iPSC neuronal models of synucleinopathy and lysosomal dysfunction. These compounds target glucosylceramide synthesis to reduce glycosphingolipid accumulation, a mechanism implicated in Parkinson's disease biology.

papers.title: Glucosylceramide depletion disrupts endolysosomal function in GBA-linked Parkinson’s fibroblasts?
papers.summary: The paper reports that N370S and L444P GBA1-linked Parkinson’s fibroblasts have increased endolysosomal pH and size despite an absence of glucolipid storage, consistent with depletion of ER/cytosolic glucosylceramide. The soluble glucosylceramide analogue adaGlcCer reversed these endolysosomal abnormalities, while the paper presents imino sugar inhibition of GBA2 as prior mechanistic evidence for correcting non-lysosomal glucosylceramide-related dysfunction.

papers.title: Plasma lysosphingomyelin demonstrates great potential as a diagnostic biomarker for Niemann-Pick disease type C in a retrospective study.
papers.summary: This study validates an LC-MS/MS assay for plasma lysosphingomyelin (SPC) and glucosylsphingosine (GlcSph) and shows that both biomarkers are elevated in Niemann-Pick disease type C (NP-C), with SPC providing strong diagnostic discrimination. Miglustat, identified as a glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, was associated with lower plasma GlcSph, but the treatment comparison was not statistically significant and no strong treatment effect on SPC was observed.

papers.title: The lysosomal disease caused by mutant VPS33A.
papers.summary: In fibroblasts from patients with VPS33A-related MPS plus syndrome, the p.R498W variant destabilized VPS33A, disrupted HOPS/CORVET-dependent lactosylceramide trafficking, and caused endosomal/lysosomal abnormalities. Bortezomib stabilized mutant VPS33A, while 50 nM eliglustat partially corrected trafficking by inhibiting glucosylceramide synthesis; miglustat improved trafficking in only one of two patient fibroblast lines.

papers.title: Modest improvement of metabolic and behavioral deficits with long-term ambroxol treatment in a Pink1<sup>-/-</sup>SNCA<sup>A53T</sup> double mutant mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Long-term ambroxol produced modest, partly transient benefits in a Pink1−/−SNCAA53T mouse model of Parkinson’s disease, including reduced brain GlcCer 16:0 and αSyn pathology, but did not broadly correct glucosyl-sphingolipid dysregulation. The study also cites clinical and mouse evidence that ambroxol improves outcomes in Gaucher disease, while its own data show lysosomal trapping, increased sphingolipids, and adverse mitochondrial and sulfatide effects that limit transfer.

papers.title: A novel glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor attenuates alpha synuclein pathology and lysosomal dysfunction in preclinical models of synucleinopathy.
papers.summary: The paper shows that inhibiting glucosylceramide synthase with the small molecule BZ1 lowers glycosphingolipid concentrations and reduces α-synuclein pathology in rodent primary-neuron and mouse models. BZ1 also rescues lysosomal deficits associated with the D409V GBA1 mutation and α-synuclein fibril exposure and attenuates dopamine-neuron neurodegeneration.

papers.title: DJ-1 protects cell death from a mitochondrial oxidative stress due to GBA1 deficiency.
papers.summary: The paper shows that GBA1 deficiency in SH-SY5Y cells increases PARK7/DJ-1 expression and cellular reactive oxygen species while increasing antioxidant defenses and susceptibility to H2O2-induced cell death. In Gba1 L444P heterozygous mice crossed with Park7 knockout mice, dopaminergic neurons in the midbrain are reduced and mild motor dysfunction occurs; the study does not report outcomes for glucosylsphingosine or establish a Gaucher disease treatment effect.

papers.title: Neuronopathic GBA1 L444P mutation accelerates Glucosylsphingosine levels and formation of hippocampal alpha-synuclein inclusions
papers.summary: In GBA1 +/L444P mice, the GBA1 L444P mutation reduced glucocerebrosidase activity and increased brain and serum glucosylsphingosine while promoting hippocampal alpha-synuclein inclusions and impaired fear conditioning. A glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor prevented the loss of cortical alpha-synuclein inclusions but did not prevent loss of dopamine neurons, identifying an intervention that acts upstream of glucosylsphingosine-related pathology.

papers.title: Current and Investigational Therapeutics for Fabry Disease.
papers.summary: This review describes Fabry disease as an α-galactosidase deficiency causing lysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (GB-3) and evaluates enzyme replacement, chaperone, gene, mRNA, and substrate-reduction approaches. The most directly transferable mechanism for Gaucher disease is inhibition of glucosylceramide synthase to reduce upstream glycosphingolipid production, including GB-3; lucerastat and venglustat are discussed as Fabry disease substrate-reduction therapies.

papers.title: Iminosugar-based inhibitors of glucosylceramide synthase increase brain glycosphingolipids and survival in a mouse model of Sandhoff disease.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of Sandhoff disease, the iminosugar glucosylceramide synthase inhibitors Genz-529468 and NB-DNJ reduced visceral GM2 accumulation, delayed motor impairment, reduced brain histopathology, and increased survival. However, both inhibitors increased brain glucosylceramide and other glycosphingolipids rather than reducing them, indicating that the observed benefits may arise from off-target effects, including possible Gba2 inhibition, rather than CNS substrate reduction; the paper does not study glucosylsphingosine.

papers.title: Selective Targeting of the Interconversion between Glucosylceramide and Ceramide by Scaffold Tailoring of Iminosugar Inhibitors.
papers.summary: The paper identifies C-octyl piperidine 6b and O-heptyl DIX 8 as potent inhibitors and pharmacological chaperones of acid β-glucocerebrosidase (GBA). In homozygous N370S Gaucher disease fibroblasts, 100 nM 6b increased GBA activity approximately threefold after 72 hours, while providing little or no enhancement at 10 nM and a smaller response at 1 μM.

papers.title: A dual-functional substrate for quantitation of substrate levels and GCase activity in living cells.
papers.summary: The paper develops LysoRF-GBA, a dual-emissive fluorescent substrate that simultaneously quantifies intracellular intact substrate and lysosomal β-glucocerebrosidase (GCase) activity in living cells. The assay selectively reports GCase turnover, detects inhibition or genetic loss of GBA1, distinguishes GCase inhibition from impaired substrate uptake, and demonstrates rescue of GBA1-knockout cells by Cerezyme.

papers.title: Replacement therapy for inherited enzyme deficiency--macrophage-targeted glucocerebrosidase for Gaucher's disease.
papers.summary: A 9- to 12-month clinical trial found that intravenous macrophage-targeted human placental glucocerebrosidase produced hematologic and visceral improvement in 12 patients with type 1 Gaucher's disease. Splenic and hepatic volumes decreased rapidly, whereas skeletal responses were slower and only early improvement was observed in three patients.

papers.title: Neonatal screening for lysosomal storage disorders: feasibility and incidence from a nationwide study in Austria.
papers.summary: This nationwide Austrian newborn-screening study showed that a multiplex lysosomal enzyme assay and follow-up genetic mutation analysis could be applied successfully to dried blood spots from 34,736 newborns. Gaucher disease was detected by screening acid β-glucocerebrosidase activity, but the overall positive predictive value was only 50% and most mutations detected were associated with late-onset phenotypes.

papers.title: Effects of pH and iminosugar pharmacological chaperones on lysosomal glycosidase structure and stability.
papers.summary: Biophysical experiments with recombinant human enzymes showed that acid β-glucosidase is more stable and active at lysosomal pH, while isofagomine increases its thermostability, particularly at endoplasmic-reticulum pH. Parallel data showed that deoxygalactonijirimycin stabilizes acid-α-galactosidase, and prior work summarized by the paper indicated that isofagomine increases trafficking and cellular levels of the N370S acid β-glucosidase mutant in Gaucher patient-derived fibroblasts.

papers.title: Fluorescence-quenched substrates for live cell imaging of human glucocerebrosidase activity.
papers.summary: This paper describes fluorescence-quenched substrates that monitor endogenous human glucocerebrosidase activity in live cells and localize the activity to lysosomes. The substrates also enable assessment of GCase inhibition and are proposed as tools for optimizing small-molecule chaperone therapies.

papers.title: The Molecular Basis of Chemical Chaperone Therapy for Oculocutaneous Albinism Type 1A.
papers.summary: The study shows that four missense mutant tyrosinases causing oculocutaneous albinism type 1A are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum, whereas H211Y mutant tyrosinase is partially transported to the Golgi apparatus. A low-dose tyrosinase inhibitor used as a chemical chaperone restored activity of P431L mutant tyrosinase in HeLa cells in a dose-dependent manner.

papers.title: Distinct proteostasis states drive pharmacologic chaperone susceptibility for cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator misfolding mutants.
papers.summary: The study shows that pharmacological-chaperone responsiveness of misfolded CFTR variants is determined by distinct proteostasis states, including differential engagement of translation, folding, proteasomal-degradation, autophagy, trafficking, and endocytosis machinery. TMT-based AP-MS measured these interactions, and perturbing proteasomal or lysosomal degradation revealed that effective correction of hyperresponsive P67L and L206W CFTR requires active proteasomal degradation, providing a transferable framework for identifying correctable ER proteostasis defects.

papers.title: The effect of the chemical chaperone 4-phenylbutyrate on secretion and activity of the p.Q160R missense variant of coagulation factor FVII.
papers.summary: This study shows that the chemical chaperone 4-phenylbutyrate (4-PBA) partially rescues endoplasmic-retention and trafficking defects of the p.Q160R coagulation factor FVII variant in CHO-K1 cells. Treatment increased secretion, restored Golgi and GRASP55 localization, reduced ER stress, and produced a measurable but severely reduced residual coagulation activity; the study was conducted in an overexpression cell model rather than patient hepatocytes.

papers.title: Alpha-methyl-para-tyrosine and amphetamine ameliorate hyperactivity in a novel mouse model of dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome.
papers.summary: The paper shows that the disease-causing A313V dopamine transporter variant is retained and misfolded in the endoplasmic reticulum, reducing mature transporter and dopamine-uptake function in a mouse model of dopamine transporter deficiency syndrome. The HSP70 inhibitor pifithrin-μ increased mature dopamine transporter in the midbrain but did not produce striatal rescue or behavioral improvement, while noribogaine failed to rescue transporter expression; alpha-methyl-para-tyrosine and amphetamine reduced hyperactivity without correcting the trafficking defect.

papers.title: Celastrol regulates the oligomeric state and chaperone activity of αB-crystallin linked with protein homeostasis in the lens.
papers.summary: Celastrol bound to αB-crystallin, promoted its formation into large oligomers, and increased its chaperone-like activity. In recombinant-protein and cell-based experiments, the celastrol–αB-crystallin complex reduced aggregation or improved thermal stability of cataract-associated βA3-G91del and αB-R120G proteins, but the study did not test the transfer-relevant mechanism of endoplasmic reticulum retention of glucosylceramidase.

papers.title: Exploring the binding sites of VRT534 at Cx26 as a putative chemical chaperone for targeted treatment of hereditary hearing disorders.
papers.summary: VRT534 selectively restored channel activity of connexin 26 variants L90P and R184P in HeLa cells, whereas F161S was not rescued; docking suggested allosteric binding near the channel pore. The study provides a chemical-chaperone and high-throughput electrophysiology strategy transferable to proteostasis disorders, but it did not investigate endoplasmic reticulum retention of glucosylceramidase or Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Natural-History Mapping of Lysosomal Storage Disorders (LSDs): Gaucher Disease as a Model for Precision Care.
unread.why: This review identifies concrete Gaucher-focused resources and methods for biomarker screening, molecular characterization, longitudinal phenotyping, and external-control development, supported by extensive registry and literature evidence.

unread.title: Eye movement biomarkers allow for the definition of phenotypes in Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: The study validates reproducible eye-movement measurements in 39 type 1, 21 type 3, and 35 control participants as biomarkers and clinical-trial phenotype measures for neuronopathic Gaucher disease.

unread.title: In-depth phenotyping for clinical stratification of Gaucher disease.
unread.why: A 250-patient longitudinal cohort and central bioresource provide deep clinical, molecular, radiological, and quality-of-life measures that stratify Gaucher endotypes and treatment-associated outcomes.

unread.title: Clinical Outcomes of Patients with Chronic Neuropathic Form of Gaucher Disease in the Spanish Real-World Setting: A Retrospective Study.
unread.why: The multicenter cohort provides outcome data for enzyme replacement therapy and reports additional use of miglustat and ambroxol in 19 patients with Gaucher disease type 3.

unread.title: Skeletal Manifestations, Bone Pain, and BMD Changes in Albanian Type 1 Gaucher Patients Treated with Taliglucerase Alfa.
unread.why: Six years of follow-up in 24 type 1 patients provides longitudinal evidence that taliglucerase alfa improves bone pain and bone mineral density, supported by standardized DEXA and MRI outcomes.

unread.title: Phenotypic Spectrum of Type 2-3 Gaucher Disease: A Case Study in the Balkan Genotype.
unread.why: The case supplies disease-specific outcome data showing transient visceral and hematological improvement followed by progressive neurological decline despite continued enzyme replacement therapy and supportive care.

unread.title: Gaucher Disease
unread.why: This review describes clinically established diagnostic methods and treatments for Gaucher disease, including ERT, SRT, and transplantation.

unread.title: Case Report: Novel treatment approach for severe interstitial lung disease in type 3 Gaucher disease.
unread.why: This case report provides direct clinical evidence for an anti-inflammatory treatment approach in severe pulmonary Gaucher disease that persisted despite ERT.

unread.title: Gaucher disease: an overview of clinical characteristics and therapy.
unread.why: The review reports long-term successful use of alglucerase and imiglucerase in more than 1,400 patients with Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Clinical Variability and Genotype-Phenotype Correlation in Spanish Patients with Type 1 Gaucher Disease: A Focus on Non-c.[1226A>G]; [1448T>C] Genotypes.
unread.why: This registry study provides genotype-based risk models and identifies S-MMRI as a predictor of osteopenia or osteoporosis in type 1 Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Maternal and Fetal Outcomes in Imiglucerase-Treated Patients With Gaucher Disease: Real-World Evidence From the International Collaborative Gaucher Group (ICGG) Gaucher Registry Pregnancy Sub-Registry.
unread.why: This multicore registry study provides real-world evidence on pregnancy and neonatal outcomes in 110 pregnancies exposed to imiglucerase.

unread.title: Case report of unexpected gastrointestinal involvement in type 1 Gaucher disease: comparison of eliglustat tartrate treatment and enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: This comparative case report provides direct evidence that eliglustat may improve Gaucher-related gastrointestinal lesions resistant to ERT, with biochemical and lesion outcomes.

unread.title: Management and monitoring recommendations for the use of eliglustat in adults with type 1 Gaucher disease in Europe.
unread.why: This guideline provides an actionable selection and monitoring algorithm for eliglustat, including pharmacogenomic considerations and comparative treatment positioning.

unread.title: Gaucher Disease or Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency? The Importance of Differential Diagnosis.
unread.why: A 627-patient study validates combined enzyme and molecular testing to distinguish Gaucher disease from acid spingomyelinase deficiency.

unread.title: A New Glucocerebrosidase Chaperone Reduces α-Synuclein and Glycolipid Levels in iPSC-Derived Dopaminergic Neurons from Patients with Gaucher Disease and Parkinsonism.
unread.why: NCGC607 restored mutant glucocerebrosidase activity, reduced glycolipid storage and alpha-synuclein, and was tested in patient-derived Gaucher cell models.

unread.title: Glucosylsphingosine accumulation in mice and patients with type 2 Gaucher disease begins early in gestation.
unread.why: The paper provides a disease-relevant mouse model and an HPLC assay demonstrating fetal accumulation of cytotoxic glucosylsphingosine.

unread.title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of Gaucher disease according to phenotypic subgroups.
unread.why: The study provides longitudinal biomarker and clinical outcome data showing systemic but not neurologic responses to enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Combination therapy in a patient with chronic neuronopathic Gaucher disease: a case report.
unread.why: A five-year patient follow-up reports improved systemic measures and absence of neurologic impairment during combined miglustat and enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Incremental biomarker and clinical outcomes after switch from enzyme therapy to eliglustat substrate reduction therapy in Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The study reports real-world outcomes and validated biomarker changes after 38 stable Gaucher type 1 patients switched from enzyme therapy to eliglustat.

unread.title: Compound heterozygous p.L483P and p.S310G mutations in GBA1 cause type 1 adult Gaucher disease: A case report.
unread.why: The paper combines molecular diagnosis and structural modelling of two novel GBA1 variants and reports clinical enzyme-replacement treatment in an affected patient.

unread.title: Bidirectional regulation of glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B by β-glucocerebrosidase deficiency in GBA1 isogenic dopaminergic neurons from a patient with Gaucher disease and parkinsonism.
unread.why: The paper generates a Gaucher disease iPSC neuronal model with isogenic controls and experimentally identifies GPNMB as a marker of GBA1-associated lipid dysregulation.

unread.title: Glucocerebrosidase gene-deficient mouse recapitulates Gaucher disease displaying cellular and molecular dysregulation beyond the macrophage.
unread.why: The GBA1-deficient mouse reproduces Gaucher disease and provides a multi-tissue experimental model identifying lipid-mediated osteoblast and immune dysfunction beyond macrophages.

unread.title: Progress and potential of non-inhibitory small molecule chaperones for the treatment of Gaucher disease and its implications for Parkinson disease.
unread.why: The review describes small-molecule chaperones that stabilize and traffic mutant glucocerebrosidase, with a concrete screening and therapeutic strategy for Gaucher disease.

unread.title: A Comparative Biochemical and Pathological Evaluation of Brain Samples from Knock-In Murine Models of Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: The study directly evaluates four Gba1 mutant murine models as reusable Gaucher disease models and assays for glucocerebrosidase activity, neuroinflammation, dopaminergic loss, and α-synuclein.

unread.title: Animal Models for the Study of Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: This review catalogs animal models developed to investigate GBA1 biology, lysosomal substrate accumulation, ER stress, and Gaucher disease phenotypes.

unread.title: Insights into the Value of Lyso-Gb1 as a Predictive Biomarker in Treatment-Naïve Patients with Gaucher Disease Type 1 in the LYSO-PROOF Study.
unread.why: The study provides direct clinical evidence that lyso-Gb1 is a sensitive Gaucher disease biomarker and correlates with severity measured by GD-DS3.

unread.title: GBA1 variants in Brazilian Gaucher disease patients.
unread.why: The study reports a validated sequencing approach for GBA1 characterization in Brazilian Gaucher disease patients and identifies a potentially efficient targeted screening strategy.

unread.title: Perinatal lethal Gaucher disease: A case report and review of literature.
unread.why: This same-disease case provides direct evidence of imiglucerase treatment in perinatal lethal Gaucher disease and reports the clinical outcome of nine-month survival.

unread.title: Glucosylsphingosine (Lyso-Gb1): An Update on Its Use as a Biomarker in Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: This review consolidates evidence supporting lyso-Gb1 as a diagnostic, prognostic, and treatment-response biomarker for Gaucher disease.

unread.title: [Gaucher disease: clinical, genetic and therapeutic aspects].
unread.why: The review directly describes available and investigational Gaucher disease treatments, including imiglucerase, substrate reduction, and gene therapy.

unread.title: The D409H variant in GBA1: Challenges in predicting the Gaucher phenotype in the newborn screening era.
unread.why: The study examines newborn Gaucher disease detection and provides clinically relevant genotype-phenotype evidence for counseling and management of neuronopathic disease risk.

unread.title: Is Gauchian genotyping of GBA1 variants reliable?
unread.why: The study directly tests Gauchian in 90 Gaucher disease patients and identifies its strengths and limitations as a GBA1 diagnostic and research genotyping method.

unread.title: Dissecting the biological impact of GBA1 mutations using multi-omics in an isogenic setting.
unread.why: The study develops and validates isogenic iPSC models carrying Gaucher-associated GBA1 variants and demonstrates protein and metabolomic methods for measuring functional consequences.

unread.title: Autologous genome-edited hematopoietic stem cells correct Gaucher disease and establish a platform for clinical translation
unread.why: The preprint reports mutation-agnostic genome editing and transplantation that correct hematologic and visceral Gaucher abnormalities in a mouse model, including with reduced-intensity conditioning.

unread.title: French national diagnosis and care protocol (Protocole National De Diagnostic et de Soins; PNDS): Gaucher disease.
unread.why: This national protocol provides operational diagnostic assays, longitudinal monitoring measures, and evidence-based treatment guidance for Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Bone involvement in Gaucher disease: Data from a North African registry.
unread.why: The registry study quantifies Gaucher bone involvement and reports clinical and densitometry outcomes associated with enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies.

unread.title: Patient-specific midbrain organoids with CRISPR correction recapitulate neuronopathic Gaucher disease phenotypes and enable evaluation of novel therapies.
unread.why: The study develops a patient-specific neural model and tests gene, enzyme-delivery, and substrate-reduction strategies that improve GCase activity, lipid accumulation, and neuronal phenotypes.

unread.title: Establishment of a human induced pluripotent stem cell line (PNUSCRi003-A) from a patient with Gaucher disease carrying compound heterozygous p.Arg87Trp and p.Arg296Gln variants in the GBA1 gene.
unread.why: The paper establishes a characterized iPSC resource carrying compound-heterozygous GBA1 variants with pluripotency, differentiation, and normal-karyotype validation.

unread.title: Novel splice site variants in GBA1 are associated with Gaucher disease and genotype-phenotype correlations.
unread.why: The study identifies and functionally validates two novel GBA1 splice variants using sequencing and minigene assays and links genotype to type 3 Gaucher phenotypes.

unread.title: [Therapeutic objectives in Gaucher disease].
unread.why: The article defines clinical treatment objectives and reports the established benefits, timing, safety, and monitoring rationale for imiglucerase in type 1 Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Isogenic forebrain organoids uncover early neurodevelopmental alterations and imbalances in neuronal function leading to hyperexcitation in Gaucher disease
unread.why: The study develops human Gaucher neuronal models with lipid, single-cell, and functional electrophysiological readouts that can be used for drug screening and therapeutic research.

unread.title: Clinical and Genetic Landscape of Neuronopathic Gaucher Disease in Ukraine: Hepatosplenomegaly and Diagnostic Delay
unread.why: The study validates enzyme and molecular diagnostic testing and provides longitudinal clinical and imaging endpoints for neuronopathic Gaucher disease.

unread.title: The Role of Glycosphingolipids in Autoimmune Manifestations and Myeloma in Gaucher Disease
unread.why: Eliglustat suppresses hepatic disease and monoclonal gammopathy in a Gaucher disease mouse model, while CD1 deletion mechanistically implicates glycosphingolipid presentation.

unread.title: MA-5 attenuates disease-associated transcriptomic aging and pathological microglial states in Gaucher disease
unread.why: Mitochonic acid-5 improves mitochondrial function, suppresses cGAS-STING/NLRP3 neuroinflammation, improves organ function, and extends survival in Gaucher models.

unread.title: AAV gene therapy for GBA-PD and Gaucher Disease
unread.why: The study develops an engineered AAV GBA1 replacement therapy that cross-corrects tissues, clears accumulated lipids, and restores near-physiological GCase in mice and non-human primates.

unread.title: Repurposing Gaucher disease therapy for Saposin C deficiency: Proof-of-concept with eliglustat.
unread.why: Nine years of eliglustat treatment provide patient-level proof of concept for repurposing substrate reduction therapy in the mechanistically related saposin C deficiency.

unread.title: Generation and Characterization of an Osteoclastic Cell Model of Gaucher's Bone Disease.
unread.why: The paper creates and functionally characterizes an osteoclastic cell model that reproduces enhanced bone resorption associated with Gaucher bone disease.

unread.title: Saposin C mutations in Gaucher disease patients resulting in lysosomal lipid accumulation, saposin C deficiency, but normal prosaposin processing and sorting.
unread.why: Patient-derived fibroblasts with Sap C mutations provide an experimentally characterized Gaucher disease model linking Sap C instability to GCase localization, autophagy, and lysosomal lipid storage.

unread.title: Genetic fine localization of the beta-glucocerebrosidase (GBA) and prosaposin (PSAP) genes: implications for Gaucher disease.
unread.why: Fine mapping of GBA and PSAP with polymorphic markers provides a concrete linkage-analysis method for cosegregation and indirect molecular diagnosis.

unread.title: Gaucher disease due to saposin C deficiency, previously described as non-neuronopathic form--no positive effects after 2-years of miglustat therapy.
unread.why: The study provides longitudinal evidence that miglustat does not improve clinical, hematological, or glucosylceramide outcomes in saposin C-deficient Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Elevated plasma glucosylsphingosine in Gaucher disease: relation to phenotype, storage cell markers, and therapeutic response.
unread.why: The study develops and validates a sensitive plasma glucosylsphingosine assay in Gaucher disease and shows that levels decrease after enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Sustained therapeutic effects of oral miglustat (Zavesca, N-butyldeoxynojirimycin, OGT 918) in type I Gaucher disease.
unread.why: This long-term clinical study demonstrates sustained efficacy and tolerability of oral miglustat in type 1 Gaucher disease across clinical and biochemical endpoints.

unread.title: CRISPR/Cas9 Editing for Gaucher Disease Modelling.
unread.why: The authors generate isogenic GBA1-deficient monocyte and glial cell models with substrate accumulation and disease-relevant cellular phenotypes for pathophysiology and drug screening.

unread.title: Long-term effects of eliglustat on skeletal manifestations in clinical trials of patients with Gaucher disease type 1.
unread.why: Long-term clinical-trial data show that eliglustat improves skeletal manifestations and decreases bone-disease activity markers in type 1 Gaucher disease.

unread.title: EEG abnormalities in patients with chronic neuronopathic Gaucher disease: A retrospective review.
unread.why: The study characterizes EEG abnormalities in a large GD3 cohort and identifies measurable neurological features useful for detecting CNS involvement and documenting natural history.

unread.title: Rapid and long-lasting efficacy of high-dose ambroxol therapy for neuronopathic Gaucher disease: A case report and literature review.
unread.why: This report and literature review provide clinical evidence for high-dose ambroxol as a chaperone approach for neuronopathic Gaucher disease, including a patient treated with ambroxol plus imiglucerase.

unread.title: Increased red blood cell aggregation in patients with Gaucher disease is non-inflammatory.
unread.why: The study establishes an assay for measuring a disease-associated microvascular phenotype in Gaucher patients and shows how ERT affects erythrocyte aggregation and fibrinogen-related effects.

unread.title: Real-World Experiences with Taliglucerase Alfa Home Infusions for Patients with Gaucher Disease: A Global Cohort Study.
unread.why: This global real-world cohort directly evaluates an existing Gaucher treatment delivered through home infusion and reports high compliance and safety outcomes.

unread.title: Cultured Macrophage Models for the Investigation of Lysosomal Glucocerebrosidase and Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: The paper directly identifies a suitable human macrophage culture system and assays for GBA1 deficiency and testing of Gaucher enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: Open-label, expanded access study of taliglucerase alfa in patients with Gaucher disease requiring enzyme replacement therapy.
unread.why: This multicenter clinical study provides direct long-term safety, tolerability, and hematologic efficacy data for taliglucerase alfa in Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Disease Modifying Therapies in Gaucher Disease.
unread.why: The cohort directly reports long-term clinical outcomes of established Gaucher therapies, including hematologic improvement, spleen reduction, and treatment-associated complications.

unread.title: Successful switch from enzyme replacement therapy to miglustat in an adult patient with type 1 Gaucher disease: a case report.
unread.why: Reports eight years of stable hematologic, splenic, skeletal, and quality-of-life outcomes with miglustat in a patient with Gaucher disease type 1 intolerant to imiglucerase.

unread.title: Splenic Gaucheroma Leading to Incidental Diagnosis of Gaucher Disease in a 46-Year-Old Man with a Rare GBA Mutation: A Case Report.
unread.why: Shows that enzyme replacement improved fatigue and bone pain in an adult with mild, diagnostically delayed Gaucher disease and identifies splenic Gaucheroma as a diagnostic clue.

unread.title: Safety analysis of self-administered enzyme replacement therapy using data from the Fabry Outcome and Gaucher Outcome Surveys.
unread.why: Registry data show that self-administered velaglucerase alfa did not have additional safety risk versus health-care-provider-supported infusions in 30 Gaucher patients.

unread.title: Gaucher disease glucocerebrosidase and α-synuclein form a bidirectional pathogenic loop in synucleinopathies.
unread.why: Experimental cultures and iPSC neurons define a bidirectional GCase–alpha-synuclein pathogenic loop and directly test lysosomal GCase enhancement as an intervention.

unread.title: Miglustat for treatment of Niemann-Pick C disease: a randomised controlled study.
unread.why: A randomized trial shows miglustat stabilizes or improves clinically meaningful outcomes in Niemann-Pick C disease, providing transferable evidence for glucosylceramide-pathway modulation.

unread.title: Effectiveness of enzyme replacement therapy in 1028 patients with type 1 Gaucher disease after 2 to 5 years of treatment: a report from the Gaucher Registry.
unread.why: Registry data from 1,028 patients establish long-term enzyme-replacement effects on anemia, thrombocytopenia, organomegaly, bone pain, and bone crises.

unread.title: Therapeutic goals in the treatment of Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The paper provides an evidence-based Gaucher-specific treatment framework and monitoring endpoints for evaluating the response to enzyme replacement therapy.

unread.title: CNS expression of glucocerebrosidase corrects alpha-synuclein pathology and memory in a mouse model of Gaucher-related synucleinopathy.
unread.why: AAV delivery of exogenous glucocerebrosidase improved alpha-synuclein pathology and memory in a Gaucher-related synucleinopathy mouse model.

unread.title: Consequences of beta-glucocerebrosidase deficiency in epidermis. Ultrastructure and permeability barrier alterations in Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The study establishes experimentally testable mouse models and quantitative assays of the epidermal barrier defect caused by GCase deficiency in Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Gaucher cells demonstrate a distinct macrophage phenotype and resemble alternatively activated macrophages.
unread.why: Immunohistochemical profiling identifies a distinctive biomarker phenotype of Gaucher cells that resembles alternatively activated macrophages.

unread.title: Bone marrow transplantation as effective treatment of central nervous system disease in globoid cell leukodystrophy, metachromatic leukodystrophy, adrenoleukodystrophy, mannosidosis, fucosidosis, aspartylglucosaminuria, Hurler, Maroteaux-Lamy, and Sly syndromes, and Gaucher disease type III.
unread.why: The review reports successful transplantation in Gaucher disease type III and provides transplantation indications and methods for central nervous system disease.

unread.title: Murine models of acute neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The paper develops two viable neuronopathic Gaucher mouse models with distinct timing and cellular origins of neurodegeneration.

unread.title: Glucosylsphingosine is a key biomarker of Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The study validates plasma glucosylsphingosine as a quantitative Gaucher biomarker whose levels change with enzyme replacement or substrate-reduction therapy.

unread.title: Viable mouse models of acid beta-glucosidase deficiency: the defect in Gaucher disease.
unread.why: The study develops and validates multiple viable GCase-deficient mouse strains with organ-specific enzyme activity, storage-cell, and lipid-accumulation readouts for Gaucher research.

unread.title: Enzyme replacement therapy with velaglucerase alfa in Gaucher disease: Results from a randomized, double-blind, multinational, Phase 3 study.
unread.why: Provides phase 3 evidence that velaglucerase alfa improves anemia, thrombocytopenia, and splenomegaly in adults and children with type 1 Gaucher disease.

unread.title: Understanding the natural history of Gaucher disease.
unread.why: Highlights the registry-based longitudinal evidence and clinical monitoring framework used to characterize Gaucher natural history and evaluate therapy response.

unread.title: GBA Analysis in Next-Generation Era: Pitfalls, Challenges, and Possible Solutions.
unread.why: Reports a validated GBA NGS pipeline with 97% sensitivity and 100% specificity for overcoming pseudogene-related analytical challenges in Gaucher testing.

unread.title: Long-term hematological, visceral, and growth outcomes in children with Gaucher disease type 3 treated with imiglucerase in the International Collaborative Gaucher Group Gaucher Registry.
unread.why: The registry study demonstrates sustained hematological, visceral, growth, and survival benefits from imiglucerase in 253 children with Gaucher disease type 3.

unread.title: Cell surface associated glycohydrolases in normal and Gaucher disease fibroblasts.
unread.why: Cell-surface glycohydrolase profiles measured in GD patient fibroblasts differed by clinical type and were proposed as a tool for refining disease classification.
